source.title: Rethinking LLM Memorization through the Lens of Adversarial Compression
source.authors: Avi Schwarzschild; Zhi-Li Feng; Pratyush Maini; Zachary Chase Lipton; J. Kolter

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning leaves recoverable target information, using adversarial compression and prompt attacks rather than the claim's original evaluation recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper tests gradient-ascent unlearning on TOFU, Harry Potter unlearning, and in-context unlearning with optimized prompts. Results cited from other studies are not rows. It does not test recovery by a small fine-tuning set, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or newer robust counter-methods.
record.test_reason: This is a memorization-metric paper (ACR) with unlearning case studies. Its own results test whether gradient-ascent unlearning on TOFU, Who's Harry Potter (WHP) unlearning and in-context unlearning remove data. It probes them with GCG-optimized prompts (adversarial compression), Russian questions and a true-vs-wrong loss comparison. It uses different methods from the originals, aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but the paper's main aim is to propose ACR as a memorization definition; the unlearning results are case studies. The authors conclude that completion-based tests give an illusion of compliance. In-context unlearning and WHP leave data compressible, at levels 'not much smaller' than the original model. They call the WHP unlearning 'not successful'. On TOFU, compression still detects forget data after exact completion has vanished.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates existing unlearning interventions, including TOFU gradient ascent and Harry Potter unlearning, using adversarial compression and prompt attacks rather than relying on completion tests alone.
record.method_sensitivity: In-context abstention prompts did not prevent optimized prompt elicitation; Harry Potter knowledge remained answerable when questions were posed in Russian. The reported TOFU completion outcome varies with unlearning step.
record.problems: The authors note that GCG is an approximate optimizer and only gives an upper bound on the shortest prompt. The unlearning examples cover selected datasets and targets; ACR results have no reported error bars, and the paper notes that its findings are not randomized trials.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy on a standard knowledge benchmark and general-ability preservation are not measured; TOFU gets only the qualitative remark 'reasonable performance'.
No activation-direction ablation or internal mechanistic analysis.
Only GCG-optimized prompts and Russian examples; no paraphrase, other jailbreaks or in-context-information attacks on unlearned models.

missing.what: Numeric compressible and completable fractions per unlearning step (steps 4–20) on TOFU, including the step-20 values
Statement that after WHP unlearning 'nearly the same amount' of Harry Potter text is still memorized; the authors also call the unlearning tactic 'not successful'

record.verdict_notes: Record version tags V1/V3/V5 were remapped to A/C/E. The 57%/50% figures are framed in the text as adversarial elicitation, but the Figure 8 caption says they are compressible fractions. ICUL is a prompt-level defense with no weight update, so it is weak evidence about weight-based unlearning. The ACR values in Appendix C conflict with their accompanying sentence. None of this study's authors' works is listed among the original sources; the Lynch et al. original is cited for the Russian observation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-chance accuracy on a standard targeted-knowledge metric or preservation of general ability; tests exact completion, compression, and prompt attacks in selected settings.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation; the residual-answer analysis does not directly establish a general access-blocking mechanism.
Tests optimized prompts and Russian prompts for selected quote and Harry Potter data, not a broad range of paraphrases, jailbreaks, languages, or in-context information.
No newer method is tested for resistance to these attacks.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Optimized prompt elicitation of five famous quotes without an in-context unlearning system prompt.
rows.note: Aggregate across five quotes; optimized prompts elicited the target strings.
rows.check: This is the no-unlearning baseline (no ICUL system prompt), so it tests no version by itself. It serves only as r2's baseline. Version tag V1/V5 is invalid.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Optimized prompt elicitation of five famous quotes while retaining the in-context unlearning system prompt.

conditions.value: in-context prompt to abstain from giving famous quotes

rows.note: The authors say all five quotes remained above an ACR of one despite the system prompt.
rows.check: Version tags remapped (V1→A, V5→E). The subject is in-context unlearning, not a weight update; the authors call it 'really a sanity check'. The text is internally inconsistent: it gives 6.54 with vs 4.74 without the prompt yet says the prompt makes compression 'slightly harder'. The direction of the baseline gap is therefore unreliable. All five quotes stay at ACR >1.

source_check.problem: Values match Appendix C as written (6.54 with prompt, 4.74 without). But the text contradicts itself: it says the prompt makes compression 'slightly harder', yet 6.54 > 4.74.

rows.subject: Llama2-7b-WhoIsHarryPotter

rows.measure: Difference between true-answer and wrong-answer loss distributions; KS-test p-value

tranche.reason: A different method (adversarial compression with GCG) aimed at the same question: whether unlearning removes knowledge.

source_check.notes: The unlearning results are case studies in a paper on a memorization metric. TOFU rows r3/r4 are figure only, and the Russian evidence is three examples. Appendix C contradicts itself: ACR 6.54 with the prompt vs 4.74 without, yet the text says the prompt makes compression slightly harder. Four statements cite this study's rows without naming it.

statements.correction: Llama-2-7B-chat, five famous quotes, abstention system prompt: average ACR 6.54 with the prompt and 4.74 without (Appendix C). All five quotes stay above ACR 1. No weights change. The authors call it a sanity check.
statements.problem: Numbers match Appendix C as written. The paper contradicts itself on direction (it calls the prompt's effect 'slightly harder'), but the statement does not depend on that.

statements.correction: Either drop the citation or add: TOFU gradient ascent on Phi-1.5 (5% forget set) reaches zero exact completion by step 16 while 'a considerable amount' stays compressible (Figure 3, figure only). On WHP, 50% of Harry Potter texts are compressible vs 57% on Llama2-7b-chat (Figure 8).
statements.problem: The text never names 2404.15146 but cites its r3 and r6. The study's finding fits the factor (completion vs compression measure) but is left out.

statements.correction: Drop 2404.15146 from this statement, or move it to a loss/analysis statement: on WHP Llama2-7b, true answers still have lower normalized NLL than wrong ones after unlearning (KS p 5.9e-14, vs 9.7e-24 before). Output-level loss, not a probe.
statements.problem: Cites r9 under 'readouts from hidden states', but the study has no hidden-state readout. r9 compares output negative log-likelihoods of true and wrong answers, so the citation is a misattribution.

statements.correction: Either drop the citation or add: the WHP Llama2-7b answers three Russian questions (Harry Potter, Dumbledore, Snape) with correct generic identity facts (Appendix D). Qualitative, no rate.
statements.problem: The text never names 2404.15146 but cites its r7. Its Russian-language evidence fits the statement but is missing, and the listed languages leave out Russian.

statements.correction: Figure 8: 0.57 of Harry Potter texts compressible on Llama2-7b-chat, 0.50 on Llama2-7b-WhoIsHarryPotter. Russian examples in Appendix D. No error bars on these figures.
statements.problem: Minor: the text says 'original Llama-2 model' for 57% and never says 'released'. The 'uncertainty' tag in 'why' rests only on the KS p-values for the loss analysis. The 50%/57% figures have no uncertainty, and the checklist says no error bars.

statements.correction: Either drop the citation or add: ICUL abstention system prompt on Llama-2-7B-chat. MiniPrompt suffixes still elicit all five famous quotes (average ACR 6.54 with the prompt vs 4.74 without, all above 1; Appendix C). The authors call it a sanity check.
